question: In Great Britain, which way must you drive around a roundabout?
options: Either way if no cars are there
explain: Highway Code Rule 185 and Rule 186 require going clockwise around UK roundabouts.

question: At a painted mini-roundabout, how should you pass the white circle when turning right?
options: Drive clockwise around the painted circle if possible
Cut straight across the wrong side of the circle
explain: Rule 188: and Rule 185 state all vehicles must pass around the central marking clockwise.

question: Which blue sign warns you to keep left of a roundabout island?
options: A blue circle with white arrows pointing clockwise
A red triangle with a cross
explain: Rule 185: The blue mini-roundabout and roundabout arrows showing clockwise flow.

question: If you want to make a U-turn at a roundabout, how must you do it?
options: Turn right immediately before the island
Drive all the way around the island clockwise and exit back
explain: Highway Code Rule 186 shows you must travel clockwise around the roundabout to return.

question: In which direction do all roundabouts flow in Great Britain?
explain: Highway Code Rule 185 and Rule 186 require clockwise travel on UK roundabouts.

question: Where should the central island of a UK roundabout always stay?
explain: Highway Code Rule 185 keeps the central island on your right as you travel clockwise.

question: What should you do if you miss your exit on a roundabout?
options: Stay on and go clockwise all the way around again
Stop and reverse back to the exit
explain: Rule 186: Never reverse or turn back; simply go around clockwise.

question: At a double mini-roundabout, how do you pass each painted white circle?
options: Go clockwise around each mini-roundabout in turn
Cut straight across the second one anti-clockwise
Drive over the centre of both
explain: Highway Code Rule 185 and Rule 188 require treating each mini-roundabout separately and passing clockwise.

question: Why must you never drive anti-clockwise around a roundabout?
options: You would drive head-on into oncoming circulating traffic
It wears out the left tyres
It is allowed only for emergency vans
explain: Highway Code Rule 185 prevents head-on collisions by keeping all traffic clockwise.

question: When turning right at a small mini-roundabout, what mistake do learners sometimes make?
options: Cutting the corner on the wrong side of the white circle
explain: Rule 185: and Rule 188 warn drivers not to. Cut across the wrong side of the central marking.

question: Can large lorries sometimes touch the edge of a painted mini-roundabout circle?
options: Yes, long vehicles may need to, but cars must drive around it clockwise
Only cars may drive over it
explain: Highway Code Rule 185 and Rule 188 note cars must pass around the circle clockwise.

question: You are visiting from a right-hand-driving country. What habit must you watch at UK roundabouts?
options: Do not turn anti-clockwise onto the roundabout; keep left and go clockwise
Sound your horn at every exit
explain: Highway Code Rule 185 reminds newcomers that UK roundabouts always go clockwise.

question: What sign sits on the central island facing approaching traffic on many roundabouts?
options: A blue sign with white keep-left arrows or white chevrons pointing left
explain: Highway Code Rule 185 uses keep-left arrows and chevrons to guide traffic clockwise.
